post_text:
America's school attendance doubled its crisis rate in 3 years.
15% chronic absenteeism in 2019.
31% at peak. Then it stopped there.

We have not recovered.

Analyzed 46 states across 5 data snapshots. The national rate has dropped to 22% — which sounds like progress until you compare it to baseline: still 47% above pre-pandemic. Alabama bounced back to within 0.9 points of normal. Alaska is still at 42.8%. Five states went up year-over-year in 2024-25 vs 2023-24. The recovery is real, uneven, and not guaranteed.

---

→ 5-year national trend chart — 15% baseline to 28% peak to today
→ Pick any state — compare its trajectory to the national average interactively
→ Recovery rankings — every state ranked by how far it still sits above its pre-pandemic baseline
→ Crisis watch — the 4 states still above 30%, and the 5 moving backwards right now

Day 7 of 10 · From Memphis to 50 States
Data: FutureEd State Absenteeism Tracker + Ed.gov EDFacts · Both free, no login required
The fastest-recovering states share one thing: they intervened at 3 missed days, not 18.
